confirmedFindings.summary: The window-repair pass only checks the re-inserted stop's own window, so it can push a previously on-time stop out of its window and miss a feasible order that exists — violating the ruling's §2 invariant.
confirmedFindings.detail: Verified by running the transcribed algorithm (calculateETAs :229-270 + applyWindowPass :298-352 + haversineKm :1484, copied verbatim into a scratch script). Depot (0,0); A=lat 0.1 window 08:00-08:20; B=lat 0.2 no window; C=lat 0.3 window 08:00-09:00; start 08:00, 50 km/h, 15 min service. Cost order [A,B,C] -> A@08:13 ok, C@09:10 LATE (1 violation). A fully feasible order exists: [A,C,B] -> A@08:13 ok, C@08:55 ok, 0 violations. The repair instead pulls C out, re-inserts it at the earliest position where C alone is feasible (i=0) and persists [C,A,B] -> C@08:40 ok, A@09:21 LATE. Net effect of the fix: stop A, which was ON TIME before optimize, is now delivered outside its window, and the reported violations move from C to A. The insertion loop at :331-336 tests only `stopEta` for the stop being inserted, never re-checks the stops already placed, and there is no guard that discards a repair whose re-evaluation (:347) has more/other violations than the pre-repair order.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: After the single re-evaluation at :347, compare against the pre-repair violation set and keep whichever order has fewer violations (or reject any repair that turns a previously-feasible windowed stop infeasible); alternatively require the candidate's FULL eta set — not just `stop.id`'s — to introduce no new `withinWindow === false`.

confirmedFindings.detail: cause-ruling.md §2 states "`getRouteVariants` inherits the pass (same seam)" and build-plan P2 repeats it. In the implemented code `applyWindowPass` is referenced only at :298 (definition), :510 (optimizeTemplate) and :694 (optimizeRoute). getRouteVariants (:864) calls `solveWithCostMatrix` directly at :897 and :940 and returns the raw cost-only `matrix.stopIds`; `applyRouteVariant` (:988) then persists exactly those stopIds as the route's (and optionally the run's) stopNumbers. Failure scenario: on /routes/[id] (apps/web/app/(dashboard)/routes/[id]/page.tsx:495 calls useRouteVariants) an operator picks "Fastest"; the persisted order is window-blind and no `windowViolations` are computed or surfaced — the same wrong behavior B147 describes, on a UI path that is one click away from the fixed one. Neither T1-T6 nor any existing spec covers it (T5 only pins the pre-existing variant tests).
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Run the same `resolveStartTime` + `resolveSpeedAndService` + `applyWindowPass` seam over each variant's `matrix.stopIds` before building the RouteVariant (both the per-config loop at :897 and the solver-only fallback at :940), or run it inside applyRouteVariant before persisting.

confirmedFindings.summary: The dispatch gate reuses `lastOptimizeResult` forever, so after any manual stop edit the warning is stale — and in the dangerous direction the acknowledge gate silently disappears.
confirmedFindings.detail: `setLastOptimizeResult` is written only in handleOptimize's onSuccess (:603) and is never cleared by handleRemoveStop (:625), the drag-reorder mutation (:654) or the add-stop path. DispatchModal's effect (:348-360) short-circuits on it: `if (lastOptimizeResult) { setLateStops(lateStopsFromOptimize(lastOptimizeResult)); return; }`. Failure scenario: operator clicks Optimize on a route whose stops are all window-feasible (windowViolations: []), then drags the last stop to a position that makes it arrive after its window closes; opening Dispatch shows NO warning and the Dispatch button is enabled — the B161 gate is gone for a route that now genuinely misses a window. The reverse also happens: optimize reports a late stop, the operator drags it to the front to fix it, and Dispatch is still gated behind an acknowledge for a violation that no longer exists.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Clear `lastOptimizeResult` (setLastOptimizeResult(null)) in every handler that mutates the stop set/order — remove, add, reorder — so the modal falls through to the fresh feasibility read.

confirmedFindings.summary: Both dispatch modals fire POST /routes/:id/analyze on open, which is the metered Anthropic endpoint, to obtain window data that is computed without any AI.
confirmedFindings.detail: routes/page.tsx:126-146 calls `analyzeRoute.mutate` on every modal open unconditionally; templates/[id]/page.tsx:355 does the same whenever no prior optimize result exists. That endpoint (route-optimization.controller.ts:73-77 -> RouteAnalysisService.analyzeRoute) computes `etas` deterministically and then, whenever an Anthropic key resolves, builds a prompt and calls `anthropic.messages.create` and records an AiUsageEvent (route-analysis.service.ts:99-140; the metering is asserted by the existing 'records a tenant-tagged AiUsageEvent' spec). Consequences per modal open, not per dispatch: (a) a billed LLM call and a metered usage row for data the modal never reads beyond `etas`; (b) multi-second latency during which `lateStops` is [] so `needsAcknowledge` is false and the operator can dispatch past the gate; (c) the endpoint carries @Throttle({ttl:60_000, limit:10}) shared with optimize/variants, so an operator dispatching a morning's routes from the list page can exhaust it and the analyze silently 429s.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Read the window signal from a non-AI source — e.g. an `etas`-only response/flag on the analyze endpoint, or reuse the optimize result's windowViolations — instead of invoking the Anthropic-backed analysis to open a modal.

confirmedFindings.summary: The late-stop warning is computed against a departure time that is not the one being dispatched: it never recomputes when the operator edits Departure Time, and on re-open it sends the previous session's value.
confirmedFindings.detail: The analyze effect's deps are `[open, routeId]` (:146), while the new Departure Time input (:222-233) writes `startTime` and `handleDispatch` (:151-157) sends that same `startTime` to createRun. Failure scenario 1: operator opens Dispatch (analysis runs at the tenant default 08:00, no late stops), types 18:00 as the departure, and dispatches — every windowed stop is late, and no warning ever appeared or gated the button. Failure scenario 2: operator opens the modal, sets 16:00, cancels; on the next open the reset effect (:120-127, declared first) queues startTime back to the tenant default, but the analyze effect in the SAME commit reads the stale closure value "16:00" and analyzes at 16:00 while the form shows 08:00 — the warning list describes a departure the operator cannot see. The templates modal has the same class of mismatch: it passes no startTime at all (:355-358) and its `lastOptimizeResult` was computed at the tenant default.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Include `startTime` in the analyze effect's dependency list (debounced) so the warning tracks the field the operator is actually dispatching with, and read it from state after the reset rather than from the open-render closure.

confirmedFindings.summary: Mid-run re-optimization evaluates delivery windows against the run's original scheduled departure, so a driver optimizing from their current GPS gets window verdicts that are wrong by however long they have been on the road.
confirmedFindings.detail: optimizeRoute resolves `startTime = await this.resolveStartTime(undefined, run.startTime)` (:576) and passes it to applyWindowPass (:694-700) together with `start ?? null`, where `start = origin ?? depot` (:658). The controller explicitly supports `origin` as the driver's current GPS mid-run (route-optimization.controller.ts:35-44, @Roles(OPERATOR, DRIVER), and the comment at :655-657 says so). Failure scenario: a run departs 08:00, the driver re-optimizes at 12:30 from their current location; every ETA is computed as if the vehicle left that location at 08:00, so afternoon windows look comfortably reachable, `windowViolations` comes back empty (a false all-clear the toast and dispatch gate then trust), and — where the stale clock does flag something — the persisted stop order is reordered on ETAs that are hours off. Before this change the run order was cost-only, so the stale clock could not move stops.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: When `origin` is supplied, resolve the window-pass clock from the current time (or an explicit `startTime` on the optimize body) rather than the run's snapshotted departure — or skip the repair and report violations only.

confirmedFindings.summary: The new API tests only exercise routes with a single windowed stop, so the multi-stop re-insertion loop — the only non-trivial new algorithm — has no test, which is why the repair regression above ships green.
confirmedFindings.detail: T1 (:517) has one windowed stop among three; T2 (:559) is a one-stop route; T3 (:606) has no windows at all. Nothing exercises two or more windowed stops, so no test covers: the `violatingStops` ascending-windowEnd sort (:325-327), the multi-iteration insertion loop, or the final re-evaluation returning a DIFFERENT stop than the one repaired. A three-stop fixture with two windowed stops (A window 08:00-08:20 at lat 0.1, C window 08:00-09:00 at lat 0.3, B unwindowed at lat 0.2) fails today — it persists [C,A,B] with A late — and would have caught the blocker. Separately, `analyzeRouteRun` (route-analysis.service.ts:242, changed by this diff) has no test at all: swapping the helper's arguments there (`resolveStartTime(run.startTime, startTime)`) would silently make an operator-supplied startTime lose to the run snapshot and the suite would stay green, since T6 only covers `analyzeRoute`.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Add a two-windowed-stop optimize test asserting no stop that was within its window before the pass is outside it after, plus a route-run analyze test pinning the explicit-override precedence.

confirmedFindings.summary: `lateStopsFromOptimize` / `lateStopsFromAnalysis` are exported from a Next.js App Router `page.tsx`, which Next's generated route types reject as invalid page exports.
confirmedFindings.detail: Next 14.2.35's type-guard generator (node_modules/next/dist/build/webpack/plugins/next-types-plugin/index.js:36-56) emits `checkFields<Diff<{ default: Function; config?; generateStaticParams?; revalidate?; dynamic?; ...; metadata?; generateMetadata?; viewport?; generateViewport? }, TEntry, ''>>()` where `Diff` is `Omit<TEntry, keyof Base>` and `checkFields` requires every remaining key to be `never` — so any extra value export from a page module is a TS2344 rendered as 'Page "..." does not match the required types of a Next.js Page'. apps/web/tsconfig.json includes `.next/types/**/*.ts`, so `npm run build -w apps/web` followed by `npm run check-types` (or a turbo cache restore of the `.next/**` build output) turns the typecheck red on a tree that is otherwise green. Every other named export from a page.tsx in this repo is a recognized segment config (`dynamic`, `metadata`) — this is the only arbitrary one. Not reproduced by running `next build` in this session (next.config.mjs sets `typescript.ignoreBuildErrors: true`, and CI's `npm run verify` never builds web first, so the deploy build and current CI are unaffected).
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Move both helpers and the `LateStop` interface into a sibling module (e.g. app/(dashboard)/routes/_components/late-stops.ts) and import them from both dispatch modals — which also removes the duplicated LateStop/label logic re-declared at apps/web/app/(dashboard)/routes/page.tsx:84-87,132-143.

confirmedFindings.summary: The analyze mutation has no onError, so any failure of the feasibility read leaves the dispatch gate silently open.
confirmedFindings.detail: routes/page.tsx:128-145 and templates/[id]/page.tsx:355-358 pass only `onSuccess`. On a 429 from the shared OPTIMIZE_THROTTLE (10/60s, route-optimization.controller.ts:9), a 403 from AddonGuard, or any 5xx, `lateStops` stays `[]`, `needsAcknowledge` is false, and the modal renders exactly like a route with no window problems — the operator gets a clean Dispatch button and no indication the check never ran. A warning gate that fails open should say so.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Add an onError that surfaces an inline 'couldn't check delivery windows' notice (and decide deliberately whether that state gates Dispatch).

confirmedFindings.summary: `withinWindow` is false for arriving BEFORE the window opens, so early arrivals are now reported and rendered as 'misses its window' and gate dispatch.
confirmedFindings.detail: calculateETAs sets `withinWindow = arrivalSec >= windowStartSec && arrivalSec <= windowEndSec` (:251); applyWindowPass treats every `withinWindow === false` as a violation (:305-312) and the web copy calls them stops that 'miss their delivery window' (routes/page.tsx:203-206, templates/[id]/page.tsx:410-413) with a mandatory acknowledge. Failure scenario: a customer with an afternoon window (14:00-15:00) on an 08:00 route. Reachable at 08:40, the driver simply waits; the optimize toast now reads 'Route optimized — 1 stop miss their window', the Dispatch button is disabled until acknowledged, and the repair pass will search for a later slot for that stop — while calculateETAs models no waiting at all, so any order it 'fixes' this way is achieved by detouring rather than waiting. This was harmless while withinWindow only fed the advisory analysis panel; it now steers the persisted order and a dispatch gate.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Distinguish 'too early' from 'too late' in the violation set (repair/gate on late only, or label early arrivals separately) — and note the toast string is also ungrammatical for the singular case: '1 stop miss their window'.

plan.note: Round 1 fixes all fourteen findings in a single wave (the engine serializes by file; several files are shared across findings so no split is possible). API: make applyWindowPass monotone (full-candidate check plus reject-if-worse net, #0), run the same seam over both getRouteVariants branches with windowViolations on the variant (#2/#13), give a started run an honest clock via a body startTime and skip the pass rather than guess (#6), model early-arrival waiting in calculateETAs so only late is a violation (#10), and add a windows-only analyze flag so the dispatch modals never hit Anthropic (#4). Web: both dispatch modals always analyze fresh (drop the lastOptimizeResult short-circuit, #3), track the departure time with a debounce and sequence guard (#5), disable Dispatch while checking and announce a failed check without gating (#9), move the late-stop helpers out of page.tsx (#8), and relax the T4 checkbox locator to the rendered label (#1). Tests: two-windowed-stop and no-newly-late cases (T7), analyzeRouteRun precedence, windows-only no-AI (T8), variants (T9), mid-run clock (T10), waiting model (T11), plus REG-B147 re-pinned to the feasibility invariant with the two-phase persist slice removed. Red gate: option (B) — T4 stays a pending-deploy row and the plan states the four-jest denominator; the cost-matrix citation is corrected. Option-B bookkeeping honoured: no map/lessons/ledger edits.

fixed: [#0] Window-repair pass could push an on-time stop out of its window and miss a feasible order — applyWindowPass now evaluates the FULL candidate order at each insertion position (rejecting any position that turns a previously-feasible stop infeasible) and, after the single re-evaluation, keeps the repair only if it has no more violations than the input order and no violation on a stop that was fine before the pass; otherwise it returns the solver's order and its own violation set.

[#1] getRouteVariants never ran the window pass — it now resolves the same clock (resolveStartTime) and travel model (resolveSpeedAndService) before solving, runs applyWindowPass over each variant's ordered stops in BOTH the per-config Google loop and the catch-block solver-only fallback, computes the polyline/duration on the repaired order, returns the repaired stopIds, and carries the violations on a new optional RouteVariant.windowViolations (mirrored on apps/web/lib/api/routes.ts).

[#2] Mid-run re-optimize judged windows against the run's scheduled departure — POST /route-runs/:id/optimize now accepts an optional HH:mm `startTime` (validated with the repo's /^\d{2}:\d{2}$/ shape) threaded into optimizeRoute; the window clock is `startTimeOverride ?? (run.status === IN_PROGRESS ? null : scheduledStartTime)`, and a null clock skips applyWindowPass entirely (solver order persisted unchanged, windowViolations []), while a run that has not departed keeps its scheduled clock exactly as before.

[#3] Early arrivals were reported as window misses — calculateETAs now models waiting: an arrival before the window opens is withinWindow true, records waitMinutes, and departs at windowStart + service time (so downstream ETAs follow the wait); only a late arrival is a violation. `waitMinutes?: number` added to StopETA in the service and to its shared mirror in packages/types/api/routes.ts. The optimize toast in templates/[id]/page.tsx was also fixed to read '1 stop misses its window' / 'N stops miss their window'.

[#4] Sibling-sweep duplicate of [#1] (same getRouteVariants defect, cited at solveWithCostMatrix:814) — fixed by the [#1] change at both call sites; solveWithCostMatrix itself was NOT touched and stays a pure cost solver.

remainingFindings.summary: The new seed effect keeps `startTime` in its dependency list, so clearing the Departure Time field immediately snaps it back to the tenant default — the field cannot be emptied, and the two dispatch modals now diverge in the opposite direction from the one the fix was aligning.
remainingFindings.detail: The fix replaced the reset-effect dependency with a guarded seed effect (page.tsx:132-136): `if (open && routeSettings?.defaultStartTime && !startTime) setStartTime(routeSettings.defaultStartTime)` with deps `[open, routeSettings?.defaultStartTime, startTime]`. Because `startTime` is a dependency, the operator clearing the `<input type="time">` (onChange with `""` at :274-277) sets startTime to `""`, which re-runs the effect, whose guard `!startTime` is now true, which writes the default straight back. Failure scenario: a tenant with `route.defaultStartTime = "08:00"`; the operator opens Dispatch on /routes, wants to dispatch with no departure time (handleDispatch sends `startTime: startTime || undefined`, so empty is a supported value), clears the field, and it visibly refills with 08:00 — there is no way to dispatch without a departure clock from this modal. Each snap-back also re-fires the debounced analyze effect (deps include startTime) and resets `acknowledged` to false twice. The sibling modal it was aligned to does NOT do this: templates/[id]/page.tsx:315-319 uses deps `[routeSettings?.defaultStartTime]` (which is why lint reports the missing-dependency warning there), so the field stays clearable on that page. Verified by reading both effects; no test covers the clear path (apps/web jest is green, 163 tests).
remainingFindings.fixHint: Make the seed one-shot rather than value-driven: keep the deps at `[open, routeSettings?.defaultStartTime]` with the sibling's `// eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps`, or gate on a `seededRef` that is cleared when the modal opens, so an operator-emptied field stays empty.

remainingFindings.summary: Pinning the ORS vehicle `time_window` to the departure clock makes any stop whose window closes before it can be reached unassignable, so ORS returns fewer steps than stops, the parser throws a stop-count mismatch, and the whole route silently falls back to the local nearest-neighbour solver under a misleading `ORS_NETWORK_ERROR` reason.
remainingFindings.detail: The fix round narrowed this block to `if (startTime !== null) vehicleDef.time_window = [departureSec, departureSec + WORKDAY_SEC]` (:1333-1336), which correctly resolves the stale-clock case, but on every branch where a clock DOES exist the vehicle is now bounded while jobs still carry absolute `time_windows` (:1348-1352). Vroom leaves a job whose window falls outside the vehicle window in `unassigned`; the parser only reads `data.routes[0].steps` (:1370-1374) and then throws `ORS stop count mismatch` (:1376-1380). Failure scenario: a route with no Google Maps key OR no resolvable depot (the ORS branch is `!(apiKey && depot)` — optimizeTemplate:521-532), default departure 08:00, and one stop with a 06:00-07:00 window (exactly the B147 population this change targets). Before the vehicle window existed, ORS could schedule the vehicle to leave early and returned a full assignment; now the job is dropped, the mismatch throws, `classifyOrsError` maps that message to `ORS_NETWORK_ERROR` (:101-107, no branch matches it), and the operator sees "Route optimized (local fallback)" with a network diagnosis for what is a modelling infeasibility — for every optimize of that route, permanently. The resulting order is still window-repaired by applyWindowPass, so nothing is numerically wrong; the cost is the loss of the primary solver plus a wrong fallbackReason. No spec covers an ORS response with unassigned jobs (the ORS specs at :985 and :1310-1326 assert only the request body).
remainingFindings.fixHint: Either widen the vehicle window to cover the jobs' windows (e.g. `[Math.min(departureSec, ...jobWindowStarts), departureSec + WORKDAY_SEC]`), or read `data.unassigned` and append those stops in their original relative order instead of throwing, so an infeasible window degrades to "this stop is late" (which the window pass already reports) rather than to "ORS is broken"; if the throw is kept, add a distinct FallbackReason for the mismatch so the operator is not told it was a network error.
